recipes.name: Healthier Amazing Pork Tenderloin in the Slow Cooker
ingredients_raw: freshly ground black pepper to taste

steps.text: Place pork tenderloin into a slow cooker with sliced onions. Pour wine, water, and soy sauce over top; turn pork to coat. Spread garlic over the pork, leaving as much on the top as possible. Sprinkle with pepper. Cover and cook on Low until pork is slightly pink in the center, about 4 hours. An instant-read thermometer inserted into the center should read at least 145 degrees F (63 degrees C).
Serve au jus with cooking liquid on the side.

raw_recipe.headline: Healthier Amazing Pork Tenderloin in the Slow Cooker
raw_recipe.description: Feel healthier with this slow cooker pork tenderloin recipe — instead of a salty dry onion soup mix with added preservatives, it’s made with fresh onion.

review.reviewBody: Yummo!!! Rather than a tenderloin, I couldn't pass up a pork loin (the ones wrapped in a netting of sorts) and it turned out great. Really tender and flavorful. I did baste it with juices/sauce a few times and flipped it a couple times in the last hour. I also probably cooked it longer figuring it was in a slow cooker so... I also took a tip from the original recipe and removed the meat to rest before cutting, mixed a little cornstarch and water and added it to the juices to make a gravy. I am not a gravy eater but my hubby loved it. I will definitely make this one again!

Thank you Make it Healthier for sharing this recipe. We made it last night. We used a 4lb Pork Loin Roast. So we doubled everything the recipe called for except we kept it at 4 hours on low. Before placing the loin in the Crockpot we cut the Pork Loin into 3rds since it was so big. We hopped it would help cook faster since it was so big. For the red wine we used 1 1/2 cups of Alamos Malbec. (Our preferred Red) The flavor was incredible. We also left the fatback on the roast and cooked that side up covered with the 6 T of diced garlic. When anyone entered the house the first words out of their mouth was “ WHAT SMELLS SO GOOD? “ The first segment we served with Mashed Potatoes and the Au Jus over both the pork and mashed potatoes. We also served Italian cut green beans with diced bacon in the pot and followed the meal with a Garden salad. The meal was delicious. It is a good thing that we had the au jus as after only 4 hours when we checked the roast our instant read thermometer read 200°. (Next time we will check at 3 hours) So last night’s meal was a little overdone. Today we took the center portion (surprisingly this portion was more medium) and shredded it to made a Pork Loin version of a French Dip using Ciabatta rolls. We added some of the leftover onions in the sandwich along with Provolone cheese. Are your tastebuds aroused yet? Ours sure were. Two days two wonderful meals! The final segment we vacuum sealed along with the last of the Au Jus in a separate bag so we could do the Pork French Dip again. Maybe we will add some Pepperoncini’s to the sandwich. We were really pleased with what the Malbec did for flavoring the Pork Loin as well as the Au Jus. The Onions were perfectly caramelized. Next time we will add some Baby Portobello Mushrooms to the recipe. (Personal preference). Other than that we will keep this as we found it. OPPS we did vary on 1 ingredient. We used LOW SODIUM SOY SAUCE. That was the only change in this original recipe for this review. We don’t know why other reviewers said that it had no flavor. Unless they used less garlic, less Pepper (we used fresh cracked) omitted the Soy Sauce or used an unfamiliar red wine. This exact recipe is going into our favorites rotation 12 fabulous meals out of a 4lb roast. THANK YOU!! LOVES2COOK

Wow, so good. I had a 3 1/2 lb roast so I improvised a bit. 1 full onion, 1/4 cup catsup and a cup of charro beans in the bottom. Season roast with herb and garlic salt liberally. Place roast fat side up. Pour 5 Tbl soy and 1 cup merlot over the top. Spread 3/4 cup catsup and two Tbs. chopped garlic on top with ground pepper and all seasoning. Cooked on High for one hour basted. Cooked on low next 2 1/2 hour basting on the hour. Then turned and turned off. Stabbed with knife several places, basted, sprinkled with a bit of meat tenderizer, 45 min turned, stabbed, basted and sprinkled with tenderizer again. Let sit until almost cool broth. Turned on keep warm and OMG best pork I have ever cooked. Will do this over and over.

This was amazing! I added cornstarch to the sauce and made a gravy. I also sauteed the onion and garlic before adding to the pot to give it more flavor.
I served this over rice with broccoli and it was awesome!
Next time I will add less soy sauce because it was very salty... but delicious! So tender!

So easy and delicious! I seasoned my tenderloin first. Maybe that would help the person who found it bland. I made a gravy for it by mixing 2T cornstarch and 1/4 cup cold water. I removed the meat, then slowly poured the cornstarch mixture into the juice while stirring. I turned the setting to high for a 1/2 hour. Thank you for the great recipe!

I tried it & so did 14 other people. I also used a pork loin (3 lbs.) I used 1/4 Raspberry Balsamic Vinegar (omitting the red wine)1/2 lg. sliced onion, 31/2 Tb. Low sodium Soy Sauce., 1/4 cup sugar & the rest of the ingredients. Cooked on high 5 hrs. Left it over night on warm in the crock pot & had it for lunch. Delish!!
I used a pork loin roast and it came out tender and juicy. Instead of red wine I used a blackberry ginger balsamic vinegar, which added some flavor. will definitely make this again.

I saw a lot of reviews claiming good but bland. That's a simple fix, season! Even when trying to be healthy seasonings are your friend. I added oregano, basil, onion powder, and rosemary. Gave it a subtle flavor that would be extremely needed as its solely cooking in liquids that won't give off enough flavor.

This was wonderful! I did do it longer (6 hours) due to I want it fall apart tender. It was! Very unique taste that was great. Being on a diet, this was a treat! I will make again for sure. Thank you for this recipe.

Yummy and healthier than the other version! I have been making my own dry soup mix for years to reduce the sodium. This is tender and so easy to prepare. Great dish for those days that are too hot to turn on the oven.
Very good easy slow cooker recipe. I used extra sliced onions and left it cook a little longer. The onions carmelized in the broth and tasted great. Turned the pork a couple times and basted.

Easy recipe, but it is somewhat tasteless. The cook time is unrealistic at 3 to 4 hours on low. The onions were seriously undercooked. We added a sliced sweet potato, and it too was very hard. The recipe really lacks any spices to bring flavor to the meat or the onions.
It was the most flavorful and moist Pork tenderloin I've tasted. Plus, it was so easy to prepare
This was easy to make. It was tasty.
Nice and simple! For an even healthier recipe, substitute Bragg’s Liquid Aminos for soy sauce.
I used low sodium soy sauce and it turned out great. I made it on the weekend and stored to have a quick weeknight meal. My husband loved it and we'll have it again!

this was very bland, even after adding fresh thyme and rosemary. the meat came out grey, not appealing to the eye at all. I think it just needs to be tweaked. It wasn't horrible, just had much higher expectations
I did not like it. Weird taste
I did not like it at all.. cooked for 4hrs on low heat and pork was very dry. Taste of soy sauce was not good either.

Ehhh. I never write negative reviews but I have to say we didn't like it that much to be completely upfront. We followed it exactly and it was very bland. The meat was tender but I would not really make this again. It needs something else - spice might help.
